metadata.program: Master of Science in Data Science (MS-DS)
metadata.description: Non-thesis degree requiring 21 credits of core coursework and 9 credits of electives. Offered both online (via Coursera) and on-campus (residential). Online courses carry the DTSA prefix; on-campus electives span multiple departments.

section_1_pathway.label: Section 1 – Pathway (choose one)
section_1_pathway.description: Students choose either the Statistics Pathway or the CS Pathway. Each consists of three 1-credit courses that must be completed with a 3.0 GPA for formal admission.

section_2_vital_skills.label: Section 2 – Vital Skills for Data Scientists
section_2_vital_skills.description: Four 1-credit foundational courses required of all students regardless of pathway.

section_3_core.label: Section 3 – Remaining Core Courses
section_3_core.description: Students choose from approved core specializations covering statistical modeling, machine learning, data mining, and databases.

section_4_electives.label: Section 4 – Electives
section_4_electives.description: Nine credits from approved DTSA specializations or on-campus department courses (5000-level or above).

online_dtsa.course_title: Probability Foundations for Data Science and AI
online_dtsa.specialization: Data Science Foundations: Statistical Inference Pathway
online_dtsa.description: Probability Theory covers the foundations of probability and its relationship to statistics and data science. Calculate a probability, independent and dependent outcomes, and conditional events. Understand discrete and continuous random variables and see how this fits with data collection. Learn Gaussian (normal) random variables and the Central Limit Theorem and understand it’s fundamental importance for statistics and data science.
topics: Axioms of probability and descriptive statistics
Discrete random variables and their properties

online_dtsa.specialization: Data Science Foundations: Statistical Inference Pathway
online_dtsa.description: This course will focus on theory and implementation of hypothesis testing, especially as it relates to applications in data science. Students will learn to use hypothesis tests to make informed decisions from data. Special attention will be given to the general logic of hypothesis testing, error and error rates, power, simulation, and the correct computation and interpretation of p-values. Attention will also be given to the misuse of testing concepts, especially p-values, and the ethical implications of such misuse.
topics: Level of significance and rejection regions
Composite hypotheses for one and two-tailed tests
Power functions and uniformly most powerful tests
Wilks' Theorem and large sample properties

online_dtsa.program_section: Section 2 – Vital Skills for Data Scientists
online_dtsa.description: This course provides a general introduction to the field of Data Science. It is designed for aspiring data scientists, content experts who work with data scientists, or anyone interested in learning about what Data Science is and what it’s used for. Topics include the past, present, and future of the field; the academic disciplines that both practice and make use of Data Science; collaboration between data scientists and content experts; and the practice of Data Science in the professional world. This course is part of CU Boulder’s Master’s of Science in Data Science and was collaboratively designed by both academics and industry professionals to provide learners with an insider’s perspective on this exciting, evolving, and increasingly vital discipline.
topics: History and evolution of data science
Data science applications in industry, government, and academia
Common pitfalls and biases in data science

online_dtsa.course_title: Stability and Capability in Quality Improvement

online_dtsa.course_title: Introduction to Bayesian Statistics for Data Science
online_dtsa.description: This course introduces the theoretical, philosophical, and mathematical foundations of Bayesian Statistical inference. Students will learn to apply this foundational knowledge to real-world data science problems. Topics include the use and interpretations of probability theory in Bayesian inference; Bayes’ theorem for statistical parameters; conjugate, improper, and objective priors distributions; data science applications of Bayesian inference; and ethical implications of Bayesian statistics.

This course also provides an introduction to the Stan computing environment.

online_dtsa.description: This course teaches the principles, requirements, constructions, and applications of symmetric cryptography based on the shared secret key. The course describes substitution and transposition techniques which have been invented before computers. Then, we build on the product ciphers to learn about the modern block ciphers and review the popular cipher algorithms of DES, 3-DES, and AES. We also describe the block cipher operation modes to enable the block cipher to support variable data length.

on_campus_electives.course_title: Big Data Analytics: Systems, Algorithms, and Applications
on_campus_electives.description: This course studies state-of-the-art practice and research on efficient and effective systems and algorithms design for managing and exploring massive amounts of digital data in various application domains. The course takes an integrated approach that studies all three aspects of big data analytics: systems, algorithms, and applications. Specifically, this course covers big data systems for MapReduce, NoSQL, stream processing, deep learning, mobile/wearable/IoT sensing, as well as practical use of indexing, sketching, recommendation, graph, and deep learning algorithms. Domain-specific data management and analysis, such as those in online social networks, scientific discovery, business intelligence, health informatics, urban computing, are also covered.

on_campus_electives.description: This course provides a general introduction to the field of Data Science. It is designed for aspiring data scientists, content experts who work with data scientists, or anyone interested in learning about what Data Science is and what it’s used for. Topics include the past, present, and future of the field; the academic disciplines that both practice and make use of Data Science; collaboration between data scientists and content experts; and the practice of Data Science in the professional world. on_campus_electives.description: Focuses on formulating decision problems as mathematical models and employing computational tools to solve them. Microsoft Excel is used as the main modeling platform but the course will also cover advanced tools, such as modeling languages. Optimization modeling will be illustrated in problems associated with operations, marketing, management, and finance. Integrates topics from decision analysis and operations management as they relate to modeling management decisions.

on_campus_electives.course_title: Capstone in Statistics and Data Science
on_campus_electives.description: Course provides senior-level and graduate students the opportunity to apply the knowledge, skills, and abilities developed throughout the Statistics and Data Science major. Working in teams, students undertake a data-driven problem presented by domain experts from government, industry, or academia. The course provides valuable real-world experience for students intending to pursue graduate education or technical careers. Topics include team building, problem solving, research methods, project management, data ethics, and clear communication (oral, written, and visual).
